hints.content: In order to find $H'(4)$, we should first find an expression for $H'(x)$ (for any input $x$) in terms of $g$, $h$, and their derivatives.

So $H'(x)=\dfrac{g'(x)h(x)-g(x)h'(x)}{[h(x)]^2}$.

We can now plug $x=4$ into this expression:

$H'(4)=\dfrac{g'(4)h(4)-g(4)h'(4)}{[h(4)]^2}$

We are given that $g(4)=16$ and $g'(4)=12$.

Since $h(x)=\sqrt{x}$, we know that $h(4)=2$ and $h'(4)=\dfrac14$. [[☃ explanation 1]]

Let's plug in those values!

$\begin{align}
H'(4)&=\dfrac{(12)(2)-(16)\left(\dfrac14\right)}{(2)^2}
\\\\
&=\dfrac{20}{4}
\\\\
&=5
\end{align}$
